content: Before taking this medication, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, or to any other sympathomimetic amines (such as decongestants like pseudoephedrine, stimulants like amphetamine, or appetite suppressants like diethylpropion), or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that can cause allergic reactions or other problems. This drug may cause dizziness or blurred vision. Rarely, it may also cause drowsiness. Alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can exacerbate these effects, making you more dizzy or drowsy. Avoid driving, operating machinery, or engaging in activities that require alertness or clear vision until you are sure you can perform them safely. Refrain from consuming alcoholic beverages. If you have diabetes, monitor your blood sugar levels regularly as directed and share the results with your doctor. If you are using orally disintegrating tablets, be aware that they may contain aspartame. This medication must not be used during pregnancy, as it may harm an unborn baby. Additionally, this drug may pass into breast milk and could have undesirable effects on a nursing infant. Breastfeeding is not recommended while using this medication. Drug interactions can alter how your medications work or increase your risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Maintain a list of all the products you use (including prescription and nonprescription drugs, as well as herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. This drug should not be used with certain medications due to the risk of very serious interactions. Taking MAO inhibitors with this medication may result in a serious (possibly fatal) drug interaction. Avoid taking MAO inhibitors (such as isocarboxazid, linezolid, metaxalone, methylene blue, moclobemide, phenelzine, procarbazine, rasagiline, safinamide, selegiline, or tranylcypromine) during treatment with this medication. Most MAO inhibitors should also not be taken for two weeks before starting this medication. Check the labels on all your medications (such as allergy or cough-and-cold products) because they may contain ingredients that cause drowsiness. Some products may also contain ingredients that could raise your heart rate or blood pressure. Caffeine can increase the side effects of this medication. This medication may interfere with certain medical or laboratory tests (such as brain scans for Parkinson's disease), potentially causing false test results. In the event of an overdose, if someone has serious symptoms such as passing out or trouble breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. Appetite suppressants should not be used as a substitute for a proper diet. Do not share this medication with others. Laboratory and/or medical tests (such as blood pressure, heart tests, and kidney tests) should be performed while you are taking this medication. Keep all medical and laboratory appointments. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of the next dose or late in the evening, skip the missed dose. Take your next dose at the regular time. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not contain all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that this product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
